# Synapse 2.0, release candidate 1

**Describe a job in plain words. Synapse AI builds the agents and the workflow, you approve every step, and it runs exactly as approved.**

<!-- HERO: media/hero.mp4, GIF fallback media/hero.gif -->

This is the first release candidate of Synapse 2.0, a new major version: a new builder, a new run page, a built-in browser, a new installer and one store for everything. It's open source (AGPL-3.0), runs on your own machine or server, and works with the models you already pay for.

**A release candidate is for trying before 2.0.0.** It's what we intend to ship, and we'd like to hear what breaks: [open an issue](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/issues). It isn't the latest release. The usual install line, npm's default, Docker's `:latest` and 1.x's `synapse upgrade` all stay on 1.9.3 until 2.0.0 is out. To try it, use the lines under [Install the release candidate](#install-the-release-candidate).

## What's new

### Synapse AI builds it with you

Tell Synapse AI the job, say "every morning, pull yesterday's orders from our shop API and post a summary to Slack". It reads the sites and API docs you name, shows a plan in plain words, and builds the agents, tools and workflow only after you approve it. An API it finds is tried before it's kept, and one that needs no key is made without asking you for one. If an API needs you to sign in, Synapse AI says so. Later, ask it what ran, what failed and why, and what it cost.

Chat opens on Synapse AI, on every kind of install: the installer, npm, pip and Docker.

<!-- CLIP: media/build-and-run.mp4 -->

### Every change is shown before it happens

Ask for a change and you get a review card: each change beside what was there, code as a diff. Paste a `curl`, an OpenAPI spec or a docs link, and it makes the HTTP tool, with any key moved to a Connect card, never into the tool. A fix to a Python tool is tested with no internet access before you see it.

<!-- CLIP: media/fix-diff.gif -->

### Synapse AI is a workflow you can open

Synapse AI isn't a black box: it's an ordinary workflow with ordinary agents, built from the same steps you use. **See how I'm built** opens it on a canvas, showing where it starts, where it stops to ask you and which agent does what. Duplicate it to make your own.

<!-- CLIP: media/how-im-built.gif -->

### A run page that shows what happened

Every run has its own page: the path it took, what each step produced, how long it took and what it cost, with the result at the top. A failed step's card says what went wrong. Logs names each run by what it is, in plain words. Runs of a workflow you later deleted stay in Runs.

<!-- CLIP: media/run-page.gif -->

### Sign-offs where you want them

A step can stop and wait for a person: an approval, or a short form such as an amount or a reason. You answer it in the app or from a chat channel, and the run carries on with your answer. A Yes / No question takes a plain yes or no, typed or replied. When Synapse AI builds a sign-off with an approved path and a declined one, each ends at its own End, so an approved run never shows the declined End. Risky tool calls ask first.

<!-- CLIP: media/sign-off.gif -->

### A built-in browser for your agents

Browser agents work real sites in Synapse's own browser, and you watch every action in a live pane. You can take over at any point and hand back. Your own browser, for signing in or recording a task, opens as a panel on the right that you can widen. In every pane, what the agent did folds to one line under the page and opens to the full list; a browser task you ask for brings back a pane you'd hidden. When you sign in to a site for your agents, the browser opens on that site. Sign-in sessions are kept for your agents; passwords never are. Record a task once and a Browser step repeats it with no model calls.

When a page doesn't open, the pane says why above it, never a blank page: an address that can't be reached, or a site that turns automated browsers away. When an API needs your sign-in, Synapse AI offers the app's own connector first, and says that some sites turn automated browsers away before it offers your signed-in browser instead.

<!-- CLIP: media/browser-take-over.gif -->

### Knowledge: answers from your own files

Add your files and web pages, and agents answer from them, citing the passage each answer used. It's optional: add it with `synapse upgrade --with knowledge` (or `--with knowledge` on a new install), then turn it on in Settings → General.

<!-- CLIP: media/knowledge.gif -->

### Your agents on your website and in your channels

Put an agent on your website with a chat widget: pick its greeting and theme, list the sites allowed to embed it, and paste one snippet. The same agents answer on Slack, Discord, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp (Cloud API) and a phone number (Twilio).

<!-- CLIP: media/website-widget.gif -->

### Use Synapse from Claude, Codex, Cursor or VS Code

Connect from Home's **Use Synapse from your AI tools** card or Settings → MCP server: one click or one command for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and VS Code. Then ask from your own tool: "Run my Invoice follow-up workflow and tell me what it returned", "What's waiting for my approval?", "What did my runs cost this week?". Every workflow you offer is a tool of its own.

<!-- STILL: media/connect-ai-tools.png (Home's card with the Claude / Codex / Cursor / VS Code buttons) -->

## Also in 2.0

- **Synapse AI across the product.** Connecting a channel, changing a setting, adding a schedule or an eval: each is a card you approve.
- **Workflows you can read.** Steps on a canvas run exactly the path you drew. A condition written in braces, such as `{{ state.approval.approved }}`, routes as written; one that can't be worked out fails its step and says why, instead of quietly taking a path. You can use agents, model calls, tools, code, branches, loops, parallel paths, sign-offs, browser tasks and other workflows.
- **Agents and teams.** Each agent has its own model, tools, skills and memory. A team agent splits work among its members.
- **Any model.** Your own keys for 23+ providers, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, local models through Ollama, or the Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and Copilot CLIs you already use. A different model at every step. If a provider has retired a model a step uses, the call is made again with the cheapest model from the same provider in the same price band, and the run names both.
- **CLI models on their own.** A workspace with only model CLIs set up, and no API key, gets a CLI model. A CLI that's signed out is never picked; Synapse says how to sign it in.
- **Costs you can read.** An estimate before a run, each step's cost after it, and a hard limit per run. Usage, the CLI and Synapse AI all count the same calls.
- **Evals.** Judge runs against a rubric, every run or a sample, and replay a golden set.
- **Apps and tools.** MCP servers, local or remote (OAuth included); REST and OpenAPI; Python functions; SQL databases; web fetch and scraping. A web read of a JSON, XML or text address gives back what the server sent. A tool Synapse AI made that only reads runs without asking.
- **Boards.** A shared to-do board for people and agents (off until you turn it on).
- **Chats as tabs.** Several conversations open at once, each with its own agent.
- **From your own code.** A CLI, a versioned REST API, and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint where every agent answers as a model.
- **Scale mode.** A Redis queue, a worker fleet, Postgres and S3, for when one process isn't enough.
- **One template form, `{{ state.x }}`.** Older `{state.x}` references are converted for you.
- **Clear refusals.** A workflow the engine can't read is refused with the step, the field and how to fix it, not a server error.

## Install the release candidate

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install/v2.0.0-rc1.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install/v2.0.0-rc1.ps1 | iex
```

There's nothing to install first. The installer brings its own Python, and Node.js if yours is missing or too old, with no sudo. It asks which AI to use while it downloads, and ends with a link to open. Expect about 3 minutes on a typical connection; most of it is downloading packages. Your data and settings live in `~/.synapse`. The short addresses redirect to this release's own scripts on GitHub: [setup.sh](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/download/v2.0.0-rc1/setup.sh) and [setup.ps1](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/download/v2.0.0-rc1/setup.ps1).

**npm, pip or Docker**

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai@next && synapse        # the first run uses the same installer
pip install synapse-orch-ai==2.0.0rc1 && synapse      # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

```bash
docker run -d --name synapse -p 3000:3000 -p 127.0.0.1:8765:8765 \
  -v synapse-data:/data \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.0-rc1
```

The `/data` volume keeps the server's sign-in secret, so restarting or updating the container keeps everyone signed in. The Docker socket is only needed if your workflows have code steps. The worker and API server images for scale mode are `synapseorchai/synapse-ai-worker:2.0.0-rc1` and `synapseorchai/synapse-ai-api-server:2.0.0-rc1`. More in [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker).

When 2.0.0 is out, `synapse upgrade` takes a release candidate install to it. Until then, it says the release candidate is up to date.

## Trying it on a 1.x install

`synapse upgrade` on 1.x stays on 1.9.3 until 2.0.0 is out. To try the release candidate on a 1.x install, run its install line above on that computer: the installer finds your 1.x install and moves it the same way 2.0.0's upgrade will. For a 1.x Docker install, start the `2.0.0-rc1` image on the same `/data` volume: it imports what's there on its first start.

The 2.0 installer:

1. stops 1.x;
2. backs up your data;
3. moves your agents, workflows, chats, schedules, settings, API keys and Vault files into `~/.synapse`;
4. starts 2.0 on the same web port.

Paused runs keep waiting for you. The install log names every workflow it had to repair.

**What changes for you:**

- **WhatsApp Web is removed.** WhatsApp connects through the WhatsApp Cloud API only. A 1.x WhatsApp Web (QR) channel is kept but switched off. Open it under Channels and enter its Cloud API details to reconnect it, then remove the old linked device on your phone.
- **Code steps run in Docker.** Transform (code) steps run sandboxed, with no network. If you ran them on the host in 1.x, set `SYNAPSE_TRANSFORM_RUNTIME=host` on the server. The old Settings switch is gone. A code step that fetched from the network needs a Tool step before it.
- **The 1.x builder's agents are removed.** Synapse AI replaces the old builder. Your own agents are untouched.
- **The backend uses port 8765.** The installer stops before changing anything if another program holds it. Expose only the web port on a network, never 8765.
- **With login off, Synapse opens with its access link.** It's printed at start, and `synapse access-link` prints it again. Anyone with the link can use that Synapse, so turn on login for a shared machine.
- **HTTP tools are locked to their host.** A tool whose host came from an argument is refused. Use a `{{ global.* }}` variable for a host you choose.
- **Templates.** `{state.x}` becomes `{{ state.x }}`, and an object in a prompt now reads as JSON. A prompt that matched the old text exactly may need a look.

**Backup and going back:**

- **The backup.** Before anything changes, the installer writes `~/.synapse/backups/synapse-1.x-<date>.tar.gz`, readable only by you. It holds your 1.x data folder, logs and `.env`, plus a `manifest.json` that lists where each one came from. It's opened and checked before the move goes on.
- **The old install.** The 1.x install folder is removed only once 2.0 is running.
- **Going back to 1.9.3.**
  1. Run `synapse stop`.
  2. Reinstall 1.9.3: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/v1.9.3/setup.sh | bash`.
  3. Stop it.
  4. Unpack the backup and put each part back where `manifest.json` says it came from.
  5. Run `synapse start`.

  Your agents, workflows, runs (paused ones still waiting), chats, schedules, tools, Vault and settings come back as they were. Don't run 2.0's `synapse uninstall` first: it removes `~/.synapse`, backups included, unless you add `--keep-data`.

See [Upgrading to 2.0](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/upgrading-to-2) for the details.

## Security fixes

2.0 includes every fix from the 1.9 security releases, and hardens more on top:

- **HTTP tools.** A tool's arguments can't move its request to another scheme, host or port.
- **Transform (code) steps.** They're sandboxed with no network and no access to the server's secrets. The host runtime can only be turned on by whoever runs the server.
- **Expressions.** An expression can't exhaust memory or CPU.
- **Run data.** Code steps get a run's values as data, never pasted into their program.
- **Secrets stay masked.** That covers:
  - keys pasted into chat, run errors and run logs;
  - a key written with lookalike characters;
  - a password inside a URL;
  - channel tokens.

  A key found in a pasted `curl` goes to a Connect card, never into a tool.
- **Tool access.** An agent holds the Vault's write tool only when it names it, and never for a website visitor. A Browser agent that can click or type asks first.
- **The browser.** An agent presses Submit or Send only when you asked in your own words, every payment is yours to press, and no page reaches a private address.
- **Synapse AI's own workflows** act only for a signed-in person, and can't be run or edited by id.

## Known limits

- **Use the Connect card for keys.** A key typed into chat before Synapse AI shows its Connect card may stay in that run's records.
- **Sign-offs don't post their question to Microsoft Teams yet.** A Teams reply answers one, but a step waiting on a Teams channel doesn't send its question there; answer it in the app or use another channel.
- **Code steps need Docker,** or `SYNAPSE_TRANSFORM_RUNTIME=host` on a machine you trust.
- **WhatsApp is the Cloud API only.** There's no QR sign-in in 2.0.
- **Knowledge is an add-on.** Add it with `synapse upgrade --with knowledge`, then turn it on in Settings → General.
- **The Docker images are larger than they need to be.** They still carry the full browser build beside the headless one; a later release slims them.
- **Model size matters for Synapse AI.** It's tested with Claude Haiku 4.5 and larger models; with small local models, expect more corrections at the review card.
